introduction: Michigan’s Family Independence Program provides temporary cash assistance to eligible pregnant applicants and families with minor children. Apply through MI Bridges or MDHHS.
description: Michigan’s Family Independence Program provides temporary cash assistance to eligible pregnant applicants and families with minor children. Apply through MI Bridges or MDHHS.

sections.who: Financial and family eligibility requirements apply. A previous time-limit closure does not establish current eligibility.
sections.get: The adult lifetime limit increased from 48 to 60 months in April 2025. Some families previously closed at 48 months may reapply for additional months.
sections.docs:

  • Income, resources and child or pregnancy records requested by MDHHS.
  • Information about barriers to participation.
sections.apply:
1. Submit the application

    Use MDHHS’s FIP page to reach MI Bridges, a printable form or your local office.

  2. Complete the case review

    Provide evidence and explain any previous FIP benefits.

  3. Confirm participation rules

    Ask about employment services, support needs and exemptions before missing an assigned activity.
sections.after: Keep case notices and appointment dates. Reapplying after a time-limit change is a new eligibility review.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using FIP current time limit and application. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can I reapply after a 48-month closure?
The state says you may, subject to current eligibility and remaining months.
No. Paper and local-office routes are listed.
Eligible pregnant applicants may receive assistance.
Does the new limit guarantee extra payments?
No. Current eligibility must still be established.
